RSA.primitive: Public-Key Encryption / Digital Signature / Key Exchange
RSA.nist_replacement: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key encapsulation; ML-DSA (FIPS 204) / SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) for digital signatures
RSA.notes: Shor's algorithm solves prime factorization in polynomial time O((log N)^3), completely breaking all key sizes (RSA-1024, RSA-2048, RSA-4096).

DSA.notes: Relies on the discrete logarithm problem over finite fields, broken by Shor's algorithm.

DH.notes: Finite-field Diffie-Hellman is solvable in polynomial time using Shor's algorithm for discrete logarithms.

ECDH.notes: Elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem (ECDLP) is solved by Shor's algorithm with fewer qubits than RSA.

ECDSA.notes: Vulnerable to polynomial-time key recovery via Shor's algorithm on elliptic curves.

Ed25519.notes: Curve25519 Edwards form is highly efficient classically, but completely vulnerable to Shor's algorithm.

X25519.notes: Curve25519 key exchange; broken by Shor's algorithm. Recommended transitional migration is hybrid X25519+ML-KEM.

AES-128.notes: Grover's algorithm quadratically speeds up brute force searches, reducing AES-128 effective security from 128 to ~64 bits.

AES-192.notes: Grover's algorithm reduces effective security from 192 bits to ~96 bits. Upgrade to AES-256 is recommended.

AES-256.notes: Grover's search reduces effective security from 256 to 128 bits, which remains computationally infeasible for quantum computers.

3DES.notes: Classically broken and obsolete due to 64-bit block size Sweet32 collision attacks. Deprecated by NIST SP 800-131A Rev 2.

DES.notes: Classically insecure; 56-bit key length is trivially brute-forced in hours classically.

RC4.notes: Classically broken due to severe keystream biases. Prohibited in TLS by RFC 7465.

MD5.notes: Classically broken collision resistance (collisions generated in seconds). Must never be used for digital signatures or security.

SHA-1.notes: Classically broken collision resistance (demonstrated by SHAttered and Shambles attacks). Deprecated by NIST.

SHA-256.nist_replacement: SHA-384 / SHA-512 recommended for higher security margins
SHA-256.notes: Quantum collision finding via Brassard-Høyer-Tapp provides ~128 bits of security; pre-image resistance via Grover provides ~128 bits.

SHA-384.notes: Provides 192 bits of post-quantum collision and pre-image resistance.

SHA-512.notes: Provides 256 bits of post-quantum collision and pre-image resistance.

SHA-3.notes: Sponge construction immune to length extension; provides robust post-quantum resistance across SHA3-256/384/512 and SHAKE.

HMAC.notes: When instantiated with quantum-safe underlying hash (SHA-256/384) and >=256-bit key, HMAC remains quantum-safe.

ChaCha20.notes: 256-bit key size retains 128-bit quantum security against Grover's algorithm.

SSLv3.notes: Classically broken (POODLE attack). Completely prohibited across all modern standards (RFC 7568).

TLS 1.0.notes: Classically obsolete (BEAST, POODLE, weak CBC padding). Formally deprecated by RFC 8996.

TLS 1.1.notes: Classically obsolete. Formally deprecated by RFC 8996.

TLS 1.2.notes: Key exchanges rely on RSA or ECDHE which are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Subject to Harvest Now, Decrypt Later.

TLS 1.3.nist_replacement: TLS 1.3 with Hybrid ML-KEM Key Exchange (e.g. X25519MLKEM768)
TLS 1.3.notes: Classically sound and modern, but standard deployments using ECDHE key exchange are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Must be upgraded with PQC/Hybrid KEM cipher groups.

ML-KEM.nist_replacement: Standardized in NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, ML-KEM-1024)
ML-KEM.notes: Primary NIST standard for general public-key encryption and key establishment, derived from CRYSTALS-Kyber.

ML-DSA.nist_replacement: Standardized in NIST FIPS 204 (ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87)
ML-DSA.notes: Primary NIST standard for general digital signatures, derived from CRYSTALS-Dilithium.

SLH-DSA.notes: Stateless hash-based alternative to lattice assumptions, derived from SPHINCS+. Ideal hedge against potential lattice cryptanalysis.

Kyber.notes: Round 3 NIST PQC winner; standardized as ML-KEM in FIPS 203 with minor parameter tweaks.

Dilithium.notes: Round 3 NIST PQC winner; standardized as ML-DSA in FIPS 204 with parameter refinements.
